newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Visa expects to grow 20 pct in Brazil this year.
newsitem.headline: Visa expects to grow 20 pct in Brazil this year.

text.p: Visa International's Brazilian unit said Visa card transactions in Brazil are expected to grow 20 percent to $12 billion in 1997 due to the launching of new products and increasing number of affiliate banks.
Visa plans to raise the number of credit cards in Brazil by 26 percent to 11.5 million this year, said Andres Espinosa, president of Visa do Brasil.
Financial transactions using Visa cards last year totalled $10 billion, a jump of 31 percent over 1995, Espinosa told a news conference.
Brazil accounts for 40 percent of Visa's Latin American market share, he said.
The growth was a result of the government's ongoing Real anti-inflation plan which has boosted credit sales in the country since mid-1994 when the plan was implemented, he said.
However, he noted that Visa's growth from now on would be heavily based in replacing old financial instruments with cards used for electronic transactions.
For example, the company plans to launch nationwide by mid-1997 a special credit card for low-income Brazilian families, Espinosa said.

This new card will be offered by local credit unions and will be destined to families with an average monthly income of 300 reais ($287). It will allow these families to acquire goods by paying in monthly installments.
The card is expected to reduce paperwork, streamline and reduce the cost of credit sales in Brazil, said Leonel Neto, Visa do Brasil's executive director for business.

Neto also expects Visa Electron card users to grow to 10 million this year from 3 million in 1996, the year the card was launched. Visa Electron allows purchases to be directly credited in a person's checking account.
Visa increased the number of Brazilian affiliate banks to 50 last year and currently 83 percent of all local banks offer Visa products, Neto said.
In Latin America, 34.4 million people use Visa credit cards. Transactions last year using Visa cards totalled $32.3 billion in the region.
